study type: Observational cohort study evaluating an intervention
exposure: stepwise administration of carbetocin (initial 50 microg, with a subsequent 50 microg if uterine contraction was inadequate)
cohort: The study participants were 152 term pregnant women undergoing elective cesarean delivery, excluding those with BMI >= 35 kg/m2, any underlying medical conditions contraindicating carbetocin, or conditions affecting uterine contraction.
finding: The stepwise carbetocin regimen demonstrated 69.7% effectiveness in achieving adequate uterine contraction after the initial dose, which increased to 89.4% following a second dose during elective cesarean deliveries, with estimated blood loss exceeding 500 mL in 32.9% of cases.
mod_finding: The study exclusively investigated the effectiveness of stepwise carbetocin administration during elective cesarean deliveries.
